facts.fact: In January 1876 Tom Allen of St. Louis was described as holding the title of champion of America.
In February 1876 Tom Allen said he had retired from the ring only until an opportunity came to get back in.
In May 1876 Tom Allen weighed 195 pounds and expected to reduce to his fighting weight of about 178 pounds within twelve weeks.
In September 1876 Tom Allen lost the championship of America to Joe Goss in his last battle.

In September 1876 Tom Allen announced his withdrawal from the ring in cards published in the Cincinnati evening papers, saying he would never enter it again and would become a private citizen after his benefit.
The Post-Dispatch called Tom Allen the champion of the squared circle in September 1876 and said he was with them in St. Louis.
In October 1876 the Theatre Comique advertised Tom Allen and Jem Mace as the Two Champions of the World.
In September 1877 Tom Allen was described as the champion of America.
In March 1878 Tom Allen was described as the Champion of America.
Tom Allen won the championship of England in 1878 by beating Charles Davis, and the paper called him the champion pugilist.
On 22 May 1878 in London, Tom Allen was presented with a silver cup inscribed as champion boxer of England by his backers and admirers.
In June 1879 Tom Allen claimed that Dwyer could not claim the championship until he met Allen in the ring, since Allen had kept a challenge open to the world and had won the title three times.
A 1903 article gives 1880 as the year Tom Allen started his career as a fighter.

facts.fact: A 1934 article says Tom Allen was heavyweight champion in the 1880s.
facts.conflict: title in the 1880s: 247.c2 (1934 article) vs the ex-champion descriptions of 1882-1889

facts.fact: A silver cup inscribed as champion boxer of England was on display at Patsy Sheppard's in October 1882.
In November 1882 Tom Allen was said to have won more battles than any other man in England.
From 1882 to 1883 the press described Tom Allen as an ex-prize fighter or ex-champion.
Tom Allen returned to St. Louis from England in December 1882 and received a cordial welcome at St. Louis sporting resorts.
In December 1882 Tom Allen said he preferred bare-fist fighting to hard or soft gloves.
On 27 January 1883 The Republic described Tom Allen as the late world's champion when he came to the stage at the Muldoon-Bauer match.
From 1886 to 1889 the press described Tom Allen as the ex-champion, or the retired champion pugilist, of the world.
A saloon cup Tom Allen won from Charles Davis in 1878 was kept behind the bar of his saloon in a glass case in 1895.
